summary: The main article describes a photoinduced radical sulfur dioxide insertion and Truce-Smiles rearrangement to synthesize chiral sulfones. It includes one optimization table, two figures illustrating the substrate scope for different radical precursors, and one figure detailing control experiments and the proposed reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Valuable chiral sulfone-containing molecules and their construction. a Representative bioactive molecules containing chiral sulfone motif. b Truce -Smiles rearrangement. c This work: radical sulfur dioxide insertion triggered asymmetric Truce -Smiles rearrangement.
items.description: This figure illustrates the biological significance of chiral sulfones and compares classical ionic Truce-Smiles rearrangements with the radical-triggered approach developed in this study.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions a
items.description: This table details the screening of photocatalysts, solvents, and additives to optimize the yield and enantioselectivity of the radical rearrangement using sodium dithionite and diazonium salts.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Generality of enantioselective Smiles rearrangement involving aryldiazonium tetra fl uoroborates.
items.description: This figure displays the substrate scope for the reaction using various aryldiazonium salts, showing the resulting yields and enantiomeric excess (ee) for products 4a through 4u.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Generality of enantioselective Smiles rearrangement involving thianthrenium salts.
items.description: This figure showcases the substrate scope using thianthrenium salts as radical precursors, including applications to late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules like estrone.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Control experiments and plausible mechanism. a Control experiments: (1) With TEMPO as a radical scavenger; (2) With BHT as a radical scavenger; (3) With 1,1-diphenylethylene as a radical scavenger. b Proposed mechanism for photocatalytic asymmetric Smiles rearrangements based on diazonium salts.
items.description: This figure presents radical trapping experiments and a detailed catalytic cycle involving sulfur dioxide insertion and aryl migration through a spirocyclic transition state.
